question.text: Let $f(x)$ be a derivable function, $f^{\prime}(x)>f(x)$ and $f(0)=0 .$ Then

options.text: no sign of $f(x)$ can be ascertained

solution.text:
Let $g(x)=e^{-x} f(x)$
$\therefore$ $g^{\prime}(x)=e^{-x} f^{\prime}(x)-e^{-x} f(x)$
$\quad=e^{-x}\left(f^{\prime}(x)-f(x)\right)$
Since, $f^{\prime}(x)>f(x),$ so $f^{\prime}(x)-f(x)>0$
$\therefore e^{-x}\left(f^{\prime}(x)-f(x)\right)>0$
$\Rightarrow \quad g^{\prime}(x)>0$
$\therefore g(x)$ is an increasing function. 
Now, $g(x)>g(0) \forall x>0$
$\begin{array}{lr}\Rightarrow e^{-x} f(x)>e^{0} f(0) & \\ \Rightarrow e^{-x} f(x)>0 & {[\because f(0)=0]}\end{array}$
$\Rightarrow \quad f(x)>0, \forall x>0$
